questions.stem: Which of the following lanthanoid ions is/are common and stable in $+4$ oxidation state?
questions.solution: Cerium ($\mathrm{Ce}$, $Z=58$) has electronic configuration $\mathrm{[Xe]} 4f^1 5d^1 6s^2$. Losing 4 electrons gives $\mathrm{Ce^{4+}}$ with a stable noble-gas configuration $\mathrm{[Xe]}$, making it a well-known stable $+4$ ion.

questions.stem: The common oxidation state of lanthanoids is $+3$. Which of the following lanthanoids also shows $+4$ oxidation state?
questions.solution: Cerium ($\mathrm{Ce}$, $Z=58$) has electronic configuration $[\mathrm{Xe}] 4f^1 5d^1 6s^2$. By losing 4 electrons, it acquires a stable noble gas configuration $[\mathrm{Xe}]$, hence easily showing $+4$ oxidation state.

questions.stem: The spin-only magnetic moment value of $\text{Gd}^{3+}$ ion is _______ $\text{B.M.}$ (Nearest Integer) [Atomic number of Gd is 64]
questions.solution:
Gd ($Z=64$) electronic configuration is $[\text{Xe}] 4f^7 5d^1 6s^2$.
$\text{Gd}^{3+}$ electronic configuration is $[\text{Xe}] 4f^7$.
Number of unpaired electrons ($n$) $= 7$.
Spin-only magnetic moment $\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)} = \sqrt{7(9)} = \sqrt{63} \approx 7.94\text{ B.M.}$
Rounding to the nearest integer gives 8.
